system.name: SING
system.one_liner: a full-stack system for managing shared ML GPU clusters via four extensible layers

components.name: Layer 1: Job Profile Layer
components.role: lets users define job and environment requirements via a self-contained profile syntax

components.name: Layer 2: Adapter Layer
components.role: interface between users and the cluster for job submission and monitoring

components.name: SING Command Line Interface (CLI)
components.role: user-side tool for Authenticate, Submit, Interact

components.name: SING Cluster Service
components.role: cluster-side service (Parse, Compile, Monitor) transparent to users

components.name: Layer 3: Scheduler Layer
components.role: manages resource allocation and job scheduling

components.name: Scheduling Mechanisms
components.role: optimized FCFS with thresholded backfill, power-of-2 allocation, reserved resources for small jobs

components.name: Layer 4: Execution Layer
components.role: executes ML jobs on cluster nodes

components.name: Provision
components.role: three provisioning objectives: resource/network isolation, environment/dependency installation, networked file storage

flows.what: job submission, execution transparent to users

content.key_idea: SING structures cluster management into four stacked layers — job profile, adapter, scheduler, execution — each independently extensible, running user jobs from specification down to provisioned execution.
content.reading_order: Top-to-bottom through Layer 1 to Layer 4, each row pairing an icon with its layer's responsibilities and section reference.

summary: Figure 1 lays out SING's four-layer architecture for managing a shared ML GPU cluster. From top to bottom: the Job Profile Layer, where users author jobs with a self-contained profile syntax (illustrated by a sample job_metadata/script/configurations snippet); the Adapter Layer, split into a user-side SING CLI (Authenticate, Submit, Interact) and a cluster-side SING Cluster Service (Parse, Compile, Monitor) that stays transparent to users; the Scheduler Layer, which lists its scheduling mechanisms — optimized FCFS with backfill, power-of-2 allocation, and reserved capacity for small jobs; and the Execution Layer, which names its three provisioning objectives — resource/network isolation, environment/dependency installation, and networked file storage. Each layer row pairs a simple line-art icon with a text panel and its corresponding paper section, presenting SING as a stack of independently described, extensible layers.
summary_zh: 图1展示 SING 的四层架构：作业描述层（Job Profile）定义作业与环境；适配层（Adapter）含用户侧命令行与集群侧服务；调度层（Scheduler）负责资源分配与作业调度；执行层（Execution）负责资源、环境与存储的实际配置。
